useCase: Malkom BOL extraction and information resolution
principle: Claims establish canonical operational knowledge only within their stated applicability. Runtime/client labels without authoritative semantics remain explicit bindings or source-context gaps.

claims.statement: A regulated U.S. motor-carrier bill of lading under 49 CFR 373.101 contains consignor and consignee names, origin and destination points, number of packages, description of freight, and weight/volume/measurement when applicable to rating.
claims.resolutionEffect: Establishes authoritative canonical content obligations within the regulation's scope; does not define all client BOL fields.

claims.statement: When hazardous and non-hazardous materials share a shipping paper, 49 CFR 172.201 provides governed methods for identifying hazardous entries, including sequencing, contrasting/highlighting, or an HM-column X where the rule applies.
claims.resolutionEffect: Hazardous Flag becomes a semantic/regulatory classification with line-item association and evidence rules; it must not be inferred from unrelated text.

claims.statement: 49 CFR 172.202 defines the hazardous-material basic description as a linked set including identification number, proper shipping name, hazard class/division, and packing group when applicable, with quantity information as required.
claims.resolutionEffect: Treat these values as one DangerousGoods object and run cross-field validation rather than independent extraction-only checks.

claims.statement: Under 49 CFR 172.203(k), technical name is conditionally required for specified n.o.s./generic hazardous descriptions and related cases rather than universally required.
claims.resolutionEffect: Populate requiredWhen/prohibitedWhen and suppress false-positive expectations on non-applicable lines.

claims.statement: Under 49 CFR 172.203(m), inhalation-hazard zone information is required for poisonous-by-inhalation materials in the stated circumstances and is not a universal hazardous-material field.
claims.resolutionEffect: Zone must be gated by poisonous-by-inhalation applicability and validated against the associated dangerous-goods line.

claims.statement: 49 CFR 172.604 links an applicable emergency-response telephone number with the responsible person or ERI-provider registrant identified by name, contract number, or other unique identifier in the prescribed manner.
claims.resolutionEffect: Emergency contact identity/contract number are relationship-aware evidence for the emergency-response contact and may be alternative identity mechanisms under the rule.

claims.statement: DSDC/NMFTA eBOL 2.1 is the current referenced LTL digital BOL standard used by this baseline and provides standardized BOL data structures/value-list families for digital exchange.
claims.resolutionEffect: Use the active eBOL contract/value lists where authoritative; do not substitute inferred client labels for standard semantics.

claims.statement: Transport/logistics canonical models separate consignment, party, package/handling, consignment-item, reference and dangerous-goods concepts; field resolution should attach values to canonical object instances before client mapping.
claims.resolutionEffect: Makes object association a first-class validation dimension and prevents flat-label extraction from becoming canonical truth.

explicitBoundaries: This claim pack does not assign semantics to Code, SHC, Related Value, BOL Type, Reference Number Type Full Name, Handling Unit Line No, Shipper Code, exact account-number meanings, exact Instruction Type values, or exact Time Critical Details coding without the actual governing schema/context.
U.S. 49 CFR claims must be activated only when U.S. jurisdiction/regulatory applicability is satisfied; they are not globally universalized.
Reported Malkom Accuracy values above 100 percent are preserved as source-reported metrics but are not treated as correctness rates until the metric definition is resolved.
